subject: Demo follow-up: proposed POC roadmap & success criteria
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Ava Collins <ava.collins@evomark.ai>, Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@evomark.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Demo follow-up: proposed POC roadmap & success criteria

Hi Ava / Tom —

Thanks again for joining the demo this morning. Appreciate the candid discussion about latency targets and the mix of search vs. generation traffic. Per our call, I wanted to put a short, actionable POC roadmap on your desk so we can align on scope, success criteria, timeline, and ownership. I attached a one-page proposal (redwood_poc_proposal_v1.pdf) and the requirements matrix you shared (evomark_requirements.xlsx).

Summary / proposed POC (4 weeks):
- Objective: Validate Redwood inference for EvoMark’s live product flows (user query generation + reranking) while meeting cost and latency targets.
- Scope: 2 endpoints (generation with context + embedding-based rerank); up to 500 concurrent users in simulated load; 10k tokens/day average.
- Success criteria (pass/fail checkpoints):
  1) P95 end-to-end latency <= 350ms for generation path under expected load.
  2) Generation quality: <= 10% delta in key user satisfaction metric measured by your in-house eval set vs. baseline.
  3) Cost target: inference TCO <= $0.015/token across average workload (including batching & caching).
  4) Integration: token-level tracing + audit logs available in console; KV-cache correctness for long-context sessions.
- Deliverables: baseline benchmark report, integration checklist, runbook for failover, final recommendation and next-step pricing.
- Owners: Redwood (Rishi + Eng lead) for runtime & infra; EvoMark (Ava + Tom) for eval sets, dataset access, and business sign-off.
- Timeline: Week 0 (kickoff & access), Week 1 (initial integration & smoke tests), Week 2 (load/drift tests), Week 3 (iterative tuning & eval), Week 4 (final report + decision).

Open items for you:
1) Confirm the eval set we discussed: will you provide the labeled holdout (approx 1k queries) and the generation prompts by Monday?
2) Which GCP region should we deploy the private trial in (us-west1 or us-central1)?
3) Any regulatory/compliance constraints we should lock in before we spin up (data retention, logging redaction)?

Next steps I propose:
- If that looks good, book a 30-min kickoff for next Wednesday to pull access, share credentials, and assign engineering contacts: https://calendly.com/rishi-redwood/poc-kickoff
- I’ll loop in Marissa (ops lead) to confirm capacity and support windows.

Thanks — happy to tighten any piece.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_poc_proposal_v1.pdf; evomark_requirements.xlsx)

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@evomark.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@evomark.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: proposed POC roadmap & success criteria

Thanks Rishi — this is very clear and helpful. Quick answers inline and a couple of asks: 

Inline: 
- Eval set: yes, we can deliver ~1.2k labeled queries (holdout) + the prompt templates by Monday EOD — I’ll have Tom share the link to the dataset. (Attachment: evomark_holdout_link.txt)
- Region: prefer us-west1 for lower latency to our dev cluster.
- Compliance: we need basic logs but must redact PII before anything leaves our VPC. Can Redwood support client-side redaction or a filtering step?

On success criteria — the latency target looks ambitious but reasonable; we’d accept up to 400ms P95 if cost targets are met. For generation quality, we’ll share the specific metric and threshold; leaning toward a "relative CTR lift" target measured on the holdout.

We’re good to proceed with the proposed 4-week cadence. Please book the kickoff for next Wednesday; Tom and I will assign the engineering leads once the calendar is set.

One additional ask: can you include a short checklist of required infra access (service account roles, S3/GCS read, eval API keys) so we can prep our security team?

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting started.

— Ava
Head of Product, EvoMark AI
(Attachment referenced: evomark_holdout_link.txt)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Demo follow-up: proposed POC roadmap & success criteria (internal ops)

Rishi —

Thanks for sending. A couple operational notes from my side before we lock the kickoff: 
- Resource allocation: I’ve tentatively reserved 2 s-instances on our dedicated pool for the Week 2 load run; if EvoMark expects more than 500 concurrent simulated users, we’ll need to up that.
- Security checklist: attaching the standard SOC2 POC checklist and a minimal access template for client-side redaction flow. I’ll iterate if EvoMark’s security team asks for anything extra.
- Eng leads: looping in Monica to be primary infra owner during the POC. Monica, please review the attached checklist and confirm the readiness window.

Attachments: redwood_poc_proposal_v1.pdf (copy), soc2_poc_checklist.docx, minimal_access_template.txt

Marissa Cole
Director, Customer Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Ava Collins <ava.collins@evomark.ai>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Reyes <tom.reyes@evomark.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Demo follow-up: proposed POC roadmap & success criteria

Perfect — thanks for the quick turnaround, all. We’ve scheduled the kickoff for next Wednesday 09:00 PT (invitation sent).

Action items from EvoMark side:
- We’ll deliver the labeled holdout and prompt templates by Monday EOD.
- Security: we’ll confirm the redaction approach (client-side filter + hashed identifiers) and share the service account details once Marissa’s checklist is approved.

Looking forward to the kickoff.

Best,
Ava
Head of Product, EvoMark AI
